headline: McKinsey researchers say the US will have more jobs in 2035 than today, but about 11 million Americans may have to move into a different occupation.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 5: the headline presents a projection as a result, the piece is the researchers' own commentary with no outside check, and the 11 million figure was already cited on 5 Oct 2026.
importance_line: What changed is a more detailed McKinsey estimate that the job market will be reshuffled rather than shrunk, which affects office and administrative workers first, then employers and training providers, but it is the firm's own research in an opinion piece and the 2035 figures are projections.
summary: In a Fortune commentary, McKinsey partners Eric Kutcher and Tanguy Catlin write that their firm's new research finds the US will have more jobs in 2035 than today, but that about 11 million Americans may have to switch occupations, roughly 770,000 a year or 3.6 times the historical rate. The same 11 million figure was cited in our 5 Oct 2026 edition from a September McKinsey Global Institute report; new here are the yearly pace, the estimate that automation could take 80% of hours in office and administrative support, and their argument that employer preferences rather than law explain nearly half of the credential barriers.
notes: Full text read on fortune.com (identical to the Yahoo Finance copy). Commentary by McKinsey's Eric Kutcher and Tanguy Catlin; McKinsey is reporting on its own research. Follow-up: our 5 Oct 2026 edition carried the 11 million figure from a CBS 60 Minutes item broadcast 4 Oct 2026, which cited a 'September McKinsey Global Institute report'; whether this is the same report is not stated.
